We got two templates. Need to find which matches our target molecule. The first template seems generic sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride? Let's examine retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>O-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

This is a retrosynthetic template: product (sulfonamide) -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline? Actually forward: O-[S](=O)(=O)-c + NH2-c -> sulfonamide. So retro: break N-S bond, form S-Cl? Wait product is sulfonamide (N attached to S). The retro splits into sulfonyl chloride (O-[S](=O)(=O)-c) and aniline (NH2-c). That matches our reaction: aromatic amine attacks sulfonyl chloride, then collapse to sulfonamide. So this template likely applicable.

We need to check if it matches our target molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id of first result (template_hash? Actually need template_id integer, not hash. The result includes reaction_id and template_hash. The template_id likely is reaction_id? The description says template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). So use reaction_id as template_id.
